title: 第9章 寂禅和行禅第10章 比斗之议
slug: 高武这个和尚太能装了

;;
“一派认为，真如本性本自圆满，不生不灭，尘俗万事皆是虚妄染着。
唯有闭门枯坐、长守禅寂、摒绝外扰，才能斩断妄念，于静中直见本心真如。
这一派，便是留在真如寺的寂禅一脉。”
“另一派认为，真如从不在枯木寒岩里，而在万事万物、众生疾苦中。
不入红尘、不历劫波，何来证悟真如？
枯坐空寂是‘死禅’，唯有入世行禅、在爱恨嗔痴里磨洗心性，才是活的禅法。
这一派，便是我们的祖师，行禅一脉。”
明心听得认真，眉头微微皱起：“所以，真如寺骂我们是‘乱禅’，说我们舍寂求喧、以俗扰禅，根本不懂真如本意？”
“正是。”智圆的嘴角浮起一丝冷笑，“而我们也骂他们是‘枯禅’，说他们是躲在深山自欺欺人，守着空寂自以为得道，实则从未触碰到真如的本质。”
“两百年了，”智圆的声音变得低沉，“这两派之争，从未停歇。”
明心沉默了片刻，忽然道：“师父，弟子以为，这不仅仅是理念之争。”
智圆转过头，看了明心一眼，目光中闪过一丝赞许。
“你说得对。”他点了点头，“理念之争只是表象，真正的核心，是利益之争。”
他停下脚步，转过身，面对着身后的明心。
“佛门八宗四百派，上寺却只有三个，这三家哪个不是‘道才法侣’样样不缺？
可惜我们尘悟寺创寺太晚，否则这三十六中寺里面应该也有我们的位置。”
智圆的声音压得很低，似乎怕被山风吹散。
......
辰时三刻，真如寺山门。

真恒率领寺中首座、长老，在山门外列队迎接。
方丈站在最前面，十三位首座一字排开，僧袍猎猎，气势森然。
真寂面色如常地站在真恒身侧，气息内敛得滴水不漏。
外人看不出任何端倪，但真玄知道，这位师兄丹田中的丹核正在缓缓旋转，真元流转之间还带着几分滞涩，正是境界未固的征兆。
起码还要三五日才能完全稳固。
真悟站在真武身侧，是个四十出头的中年僧人，面容黝黑，身材敦实，双手骨节粗大，一看便是外家硬功出身。
他是护持堂首座，化劲后期修为，平日里负责基础护寺战力的训练，极少参与高层事务。
但今日真寂不能出手，他必须顶上。
远处传来锡杖铜环的清脆响声，由远及近。
真恒的目光微微一凝。
片刻之后，一行十余人从山道尽头转了出来，当先一手持九环锡杖，正是尘悟寺方丈智圆。
智圆在距离真恒三丈处停下脚步，双手合十，微微躬身：“阿弥陀佛，真恒方丈，多年未见，别来无恙。”
真恒同样双手合十，还了一礼：“智圆方丈远道而来，有失远迎。”
两人目光交汇，面上客气，暗中却都在打量对方的实力。
智圆看上去年约七旬，面容清瘦，颧骨高耸，一双眼睛深陷在眼窝中，目光却锐利如鹰。
他的气息沉凝浑厚，明显已经抱丹。
虽然依然是抱丹初期，却已摸到了中期门槛，只差一个契机便能突破。
真恒的气息则深沉如渊，浑然一体，修为锤炼得炉火纯青。

“One school of thought believes that the true nature is inherently perfect, neither born nor destroyed, and that all worldly things are contaminated by falsehood.
Only by sitting behind closed doors, observing Zen silence for a long time, and rejecting external distractions can we cut off delusional thoughts and directly see the true nature of our original mind in silence.
This sect is the Jichan lineage that stayed in Zhenru Temple. "
"The other school believes that the true Buddha is never found in the dead trees and cold rocks, but in all things and the sufferings of all living beings.
If you don’t enter the world of mortals and don’t experience calamities, how can you realize the truth?
Sitting in silence is "dead Zen". Only entering the world and walking in meditation, polishing the mind in love, hatred, anger and delusion, is the living Zen method.
This sect is our ancestor, the walking Zen lineage. "
Ming Xin listened carefully and frowned slightly: "So, Zhenru Temple scolded us as 'chaotic Zen', saying that we abandoned silence to seek noise and disturbed Zen with worldliness, and did not understand the original intention of Zhenru Temple?"
"Exactly." A sneer appeared on the corner of Zhiyuan's lips, "And we also called them 'Ku Zen', saying that they were hiding in the mountains to deceive themselves and others, guarding the emptiness and silence, thinking they had attained the Tao, but in fact they had never touched the essence of truth."
"It's been two hundred years," Zhiyuan's voice became deeper, "the battle between these two factions has never stopped."
Mingxin was silent for a moment, then suddenly said: "Master, I think this is more than just a battle of ideas."
Zhiyuan turned her head and glanced at Mingxin, with a hint of approval in her eyes.
"You're right." He nodded. "The battle over ideas is just a superficial thing. The real core is a battle over interests."
He stopped and turned around, facing Mingxin behind him.
"There are eight sects and four hundred sects of Buddhism, but there are only three monasteries. Which of these three sects is not a 'couple of Taoists and Dharma masters'?"
It's a pity that we founded Chenwu Temple too late, otherwise we should have a place in these thirty-six middle temples. "
Zhiyuan's voice was kept very low, as if he was afraid of being blown away by the mountain wind.
...
At three o'clock in the morning, it is really like the mountain gate of the temple.
Zhenheng led the chief minister and elders of the temple to line up outside the mountain gate to greet him.
The abbot stood at the front, and the thirteen heads were lined up in a row, wearing monk robes and looking imposing.
Zhen Ji stood beside Zhen Heng with a normal expression, and his breath was so restrained that there was no leakage.
Outsiders could not see any clues, but Zhenxuan knew that the core of the pill in this senior brother's dantian was slowly rotating, and there was still a bit of stagnation in the flow of true energy, which was a sign that the realm was not solidified.
It will take at least three to five days to be completely stable.
Zhenwu stood next to Zhenwu. He was a middle-aged monk in his early forties. He had a dark face, a stocky figure, and thick joints in his hands. At first glance, he was from a hard-working family.
He is the leader of the Protector Hall, a late-stage cultivator of Huajin. He is usually responsible for training the basic combat strength of the protector, and rarely participates in high-level affairs.
But Zhenji couldn't take action today, he had to step up.
The crisp sound of the tin rod and the copper ring came from the distance, approaching from far away.
Zhen Heng's eyes narrowed slightly.
After a while, a group of more than ten people came out from the end of the mountain path. The first person holding a nine-ring tin staff was Zhiyuan, the abbot of Chenwu Temple.
Zhiyuan stopped three feet away from Zhenheng, clasped his hands together, and bowed slightly: "Amitabha, Abbot Zhenheng, I haven't seen him for many years. I hope you are well."
Zhen Heng also clasped his hands together and returned the salute: "Abbot Zhiyuan has come from afar, and there is no way to welcome him."
The two people's eyes met, and they were polite on the surface, but secretly they were sizing up each other's strength.
Zhiyuan looks to be about seventy years old, with a thin face, high cheekbones, and a pair of eyes sunken into the eye sockets, but his gaze is as sharp as an eagle.
His aura was deep and thick, and he was obviously holding the pill.
Although it is still in the early stage of holding the pill, it has reached the mid-term threshold and is only one opportunity away from breaking through.
Zhenheng's aura is as deep as the abyss, integrated into one body, and his cultivation has been tempered to perfection.
